name: C++ 10 — Practice Lab (File Handling and a Persistent Ticket Office)
description: Guided learner workspace for the tenth lab of a beginner C++ course (3×45 min) on file handling and the persistent storage of the theatre ticket office. First block — fundamentals: a stock snapshot written with ofstream, buffer and close checked afterwards (G10_01_mentes), appending and summing visitor counts with a read loop (G10_02_latogatok), bad data and the stream state flags eof/fail (G10_03_hibas_adat), then strict validation of one record line through getline and istringstream (G10_04_sor). Second block — project: the ticket office carried over from lesson 9 (P10_jegypenztar.cpp holds the base class operations, the new I/O is the learner's work) built up in six steps, P1–P6 (understanding the base and the shared TICKETS 1 file format, saving with a header, parsing one reservation line, all-or-nothing loading into a temporary object, a text report built with ostringstream, then a save-or-load main driven by S or L plus the bundled broken-file fixtures). Third block — summary test: 20 fixed questions (T1 10 multiple-choice, T2 5 output prediction and 5 debugging) with feedback and no answer key in the learner package. Before every part the tutor shows a short analogous sample from the MINTAKODOK.md collection; the learner writes, saves, compiles and runs the code (RUN button or g++ -std=c++20), and progress is tracked in HALADAS.json. No homework and no separate extra exercise set.
